| | |

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Murray's frame is that a long-shot Heisman winner has hit two years running — Fernando Mendoza at 55-1 last year, Travis Hunter at 50-1 the year before — and he reaches back to Lamar Jackson entering 2016 at 100-1 to ask whether another Louisville quarterback might be primed. Kienholz is a relatively unknown quantity: a four-star recruit out of South Dakota in 2023 who spent three seasons at Ohio State before transferring to Louisville this offseason. Murray expects Jeff Brohm to unlock a unique athlete, noting Brohm has always thrived with transfer quarterbacks including Miller Moss, Tyler Shough and Jack Plummer, and points to a week one showdown with Ole Miss on Labor Day Sunday and a home game with SMU in week three as the early tells.

*Rests on:* quarterback (Kienholz) and coaching (Brohm's record with transfer quarterbacks); early-schedule showcases

*Conflict or ambiguity:* The headline names only the player. The team is Louisville, taken from Murray's own reasoning — Kienholz spent three seasons at Ohio State and transferred away from it, so reading the headline alone would attribute the pick to the wrong programme.
